questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The selection of courses, quality of the city and affordability of czech republic

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found it overall to be a great time. Lots of good people, nice city and my host university had exciting courses and not too complicated paperwork

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: We recieved many informative mails about what to do

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were some introduction from staff who were very helpful

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: There's a facebook group called Erasmus Prague accomodation

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There are a quite a few scammers and generic profiles. Make sure to not pay anything to anyone, before actually arriving at the apartment

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I heard that the dorms were not that hygenic with mold, cockroaches etc. some places. Additionally, I chose against the dorms, because I wanted to have my own room, which was not an option

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Fairly easy access to courses and registration

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You select faculty and courses in the SIS. On the day of registration, it's a good idear to be ready on the spot as many courses get filled up quickly

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: My erasmus coordinator from CU was very helpful with questions

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all of the classes I wanted, however I had to be quick

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: make sure to have an idea of the courses you want to register for in advance. That way you can more easily register for the ones you want, when registration opens

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: All in all good courses, however I do take a little bit of an issue with the mandatory attendance on some of my courses. I had a course with seminars late friday afternoon, these seminars had mandatory attendance. As university students, I believe that we have the responsibility for our own learning, and I don't agree that it's fair that we have to attend as long as we pass our classes.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was a bit lower than at my home university, however I still feel like I learned a lot

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I liked that my courses had a lot more essays, as compared to problem sets with one solution.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Economic History
History of economic thought
Public finance
Comparative economics
Introduction to critical theory
FinTech and Blockchain

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend Public finance, as it gives a very good insight into the numerous economic problems and dilemmas that government face.
Introducion to critical theory was probably my favourite. The course is based on discussions of philosophical texts regarding critical theory and the frankfurt school. This is a topic that has really broadened my perspectives on society and the underlying structures, that we might fail to spot immediately

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Fees from cash withdrawal

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries in general, were more expensive than I expected. However I spend quite a lot on groceries since I eat a lot, so my budget for that might not be representative

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't really explore a lot of them

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: ESN hosts some events in the beginning of the semester and there are some parties. While the welcome events were a nice introduction, none of the events really fell in my taste

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I haven't really done any

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Make sure to go outside of Prague a few times. Snezkou is nice, as well as Bohemian Switzerland for example

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was ok, Czechs are not that different from Danes. However they seem less polite, and the constant loud nose-blowing in public kind of irritated me

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I haven't really spoken to any czech students

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Mostly that Czechs are quite straightforward, and do not have a culture of politeness, even less so than us Danes

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: that people are very lowkey. No one makes a big fuss about stuff

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: I didn't personally sign up for the buddy programme, however I heard good things about it. Also the welcome events are a good opportunity to meet new people

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I'm not sure

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making friends from all over Europe

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: My greatest challenge was the first few months, where I felt kind of lonely because even though I was meeting new people. I didn't know anyone very well and I missed my good friends from home

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
